title: Perlmutter and colleagues: 42 supernovae give Omega_M = 0.28 for a flat universe
summary: For a flat universe the Supernova Cosmology Project reports Omega_M = 0.28 with statistical and systematic errors, and P(Lambda > 0) = 99 percent including systematics.
body: The abstract of Perlmutter and colleagues reports 42 Type Ia supernovae at redshifts 0.18 to 0.83, fit with the low-redshift Calan/Tololo sample. For a flat universe, Omega_M + Omega_Lambda = 1, it gives Omega_M = 0.28 with statistical errors +0.09 and −0.08 and identified systematics +0.05 and −0.04. It says the data are strongly inconsistent with a flat cosmology that has Lambda = 0, and that P(Lambda > 0) = 99 percent including the identified systematic uncertainties. The best-fit age relative to the Hubble time is given as t0 = 14.9 (+1.4, −1.1) × (0.63/h) Gyr for a flat cosmology. This is a fit to standardized supernova peak magnitudes. The abstract says the team found no significant difference in host reddening or Malmquist bias between the low-redshift and high-redshift samples.
